title: Chapter 94
content:
Stepping toward the private executive elevator, Il-hyun stared at the glowing screen of his phone, momentarily stunned.

A bright red heart sat stamped squarely at the bottom of the chat.

Acting on pure instinct, he took a screenshot and saved it to his secure gallery just as the message vanished into thin air. A fraction of a second later, a replacement text popped up—a flat, unpunctuated Okay stripped entirely of the icon.

Realizing that Lee Ja-kyeong hadn't sent it by accident, a slow, radiant smile spread across Il-hyun’s lips.

He looked over his shoulder at his chief of security.

"Chief Park."

"Yes, President Kang."

"I am clocking out for the day. Clear my entire afternoon schedule."

"Understood, sir."

"Ah—and I won't be returning to the residence tonight. If I am late tomorrow morning, do not bother calling."

His agenda for the evening was crystal clear: lock themselves away in a private suite and ravage that boy until dawn. Where should I take him first? What should we eat?

Corporate affairs were completely forgotten, his mind entirely derailed by the prospect of an actual date.

The elevator chimed, the brushed-steel doors sliding open at the fifth-floor executive lobby. Board Members Park and Kim were preparing to step inside, but both men froze the moment they caught sight of Kang Il-hyun standing in the cabin.

Il-hyun inclined his head, greeting them with impeccable, polished manners.

"Good afternoon, gentlemen."

The two senior directors returned the bow with tight, superficial nods, but the dazzling grin on the young CEO's face sent an immediate chill down their spines. What kind of bloody trap was he orchestrating behind that smile? Most men were terrifying when they lost their temper; Kang Il-hyun was an entirely unreadable monster who was infinitely more lethal when he smiled.

As the air inside the elevator plunged to absolute zero, Director Park cautiously broke the silence.

"How is the Chairman's health holding up? Has he made any recovery?"

Il-hyun let out a quiet, mocking scoff.

Ever since Il-hyun had stormed the study and put a bullet through Chief Secretary Kim’s foot, Chairman Kang hadn't set a single toe outside his estate. The excuse of chronic gout was a transparent farce—the old beast was simply cowering behind his fortified gates.

Why had a warlord once notorious as a human butcher across the Asian underworld turned into such a cowardly recluse? Was it because he had too many assets to protect? Or had old age finally rotted his spine?

Thanks to the old man's self-imposed quarantine, even the wet-work specialists Il-hyun had contracted were running into dead ends. It would be far more convenient if the Chairman simply keeled over and died in his bed; at least it would save everyone the exhaustion of a bloody siege.

"If you are so deeply concerned, Director Park, would you care to accompany me to the estate today? I am quite curious to check on him myself."

Director Park’s face paled instantly. Forcing an awkward, brittle chuckle, he stammered out an excuse about an urgent afternoon board briefing.

Il-hyun shifted his dark, unblinking gaze to the back of Director Kim’s head.

The man was an old, slippery eel cut from the exact same cloth as the Chairman—adept at dodging legal crosshairs and corporate leverage with greasy precision.

"I hear your son recently returned from New Zealand, Director Kim. You must be thrilled to have the family reunited."

Director Kim’s shoulders locked into rigid stone. He turned his head halfway, offering a tight, strained smile.

"I am honored by President Kang’s thoughtful attention."

"Naturally. I take an immense, personal interest in the well-being of all our board members."

"Is that so... Haha."

"Indeed. Down to who you dined with yesterday evening, the exact vintage you ordered, and the intimate pillow talk you shared with your wife last night—there is virtually nothing regarding your household that escapes my desk."

Director Kim spun around, his jaw clenched in cold fury, only for Il-hyun to flash an easy, teasing wink.

"Just a little corporate humor. Why so terribly tense, Director?"

Ding.

The elevator doors glided open at the ground-floor concourse. Il-hyun slipped effortlessly between the two frozen directors, stepping out into the marble atrium. Jamming his hands into his trouser pockets, he offered a lazy, parting tilt of his chin.

"Have a productive afternoon, gentlemen."

Leaving the two directors glaring after him in stunned silence, the elevator doors slid shut.

Turning toward the private exit, the playful amusement evaporated from Il-hyun’s eyes, replaced by an arctic, calculating focus. Faction loyalists were still actively petitioning to convene an extraordinary shareholder summit to push Kang Tae-han forward. So long as the Chairman drew breath, his loyal retainers on the board would fight tooth and nail to block the succession.

He clicked his tongue in mild irritation, waking his phone to look at the unsent heart from Lee Ja-kyeong.

The lingering annoyance vanished like mist under the sun.

With a low, boyish chuckle bubbling in his throat, he strode toward the executive suite, leaving his personal secretary blinking in utter bewilderment at the uncharacteristic skip in his step.
Perched on a teak sun lounger, Jakyeong sipped freshly blended watermelon juice, staring into the turquoise depths of the estate pool.

He was dying to swim a few laps, but the fresh sutures along his forearm made entering the water out of the question. Left with nothing better to do, he sucked the crushed ice through his straw, repeatedly unlocking his phone to check the screen.

No new messages had arrived from Kang Il-hyun since noon. Must be drowning in board meetings.

He definitely missed the heart. I unsent it within two seconds flat.

Just as he managed to reassure himself with that comforting thought, heavy, purposeful footsteps echoed across the gravel drive.

Jakyeong blinked, thinking his eyes were playing tricks on him.

Striding boldly across the manicured lawn in a tailored dark suit was Kang Il-hyun.

Jakyeong stared in stunned disbelief as the towering shadow fell over his lounger.

"What are you doing here? At this hour?"

Il-hyun’s smile was dazzling enough to rival the mid-afternoon sun.

"I came home for our date, darling."

Jakyeong checked his watch: barely four hours had passed since the morning commute. "Is running a multi-billion-dollar conglomerate a joke to you? You just clock in and out whenever you feel like it?"

"I am fully entitled to today. It's a national holiday."

"What... what holiday?"

"Lee Ja-kyeong's Official Proposal Day."

Without missing a beat, Il-hyun whipped out his smartphone, displaying the crystal-clear, high-resolution screenshot of the bright red heart. To add insult to injury, he hit play on a saved voice memo, blasting Jakyeong's desperate, recorded confessions across the pool deck at full volume:

[President Kang, I like you! I've never experienced such sublime, incredible sex in my entire life!]

Jakyeong’s soul nearly evacuated his body.

He lunged to snatch the phone, but Il-hyun casually pocketed the device, leaving Jakyeong’s ears and neck burning a furious, feverish crimson.

Stepping closer, Il-hyun pinched the boy's flushed earlobe with affectionate firmness.

"You keep showering me with these magnificent, unexpected gifts... I'm practically swooning."

"I... I pressed the wrong button by mistake!"

"I figured you'd claim that," Il-hyun purred smoothly. "Which is why I already instructed Chief Park to have the screenshot blown up, printed on archival canvas, and mounted in a custom museum frame."

Jakyeong looked at him in sheer, unadulterated horror.

"You're... you're joking, right?"

"Should I hang it in the formal drawing room? Or above my headboard?"

"..."

"Both?"

Taking in the deadpan sincerity behind those dark irises, Jakyeong’s blood ran cold.

"Don't you dare," Jakyeong hissed, grinding his teeth. "Hang that abomination anywhere in this house and I swear to God I'll burn the place to the ground."

Il-hyun’s hand drifted from his ear, intertwining their fingers instead. He gave a gentle, persistent tug, coaxing Jakyeong off the lounger. Seeing the boy dig his heels in, Il-hyun immediately surrendered, promising not to tease him further.

"Let's call a truce and go on our date, darling."

Jakyeong looked down at his casual attire—a worn t-shirt and loose linen shorts. The contrast against Il-hyun's tailored three-piece suit was laughably stark.

"I need to change."

"Wear whatever you like. You're going to spend the entire evening naked anyway."

The unvarnished, shameless declaration of intent made Jakyeong shake his head in utter defeat. Does this man possess a single thought in his skull that doesn't involve stripping me bare?

Muttering under his breath, he retreated to the second-floor suite to pull on the civilian outfit he had prepared earlier.

When he descended the grand staircase, Kang Il-hyun was waiting on the living room sofa, his expression uncharacteristically caught off guard.

Does it look ridiculous? Self-conscious, Jakyeong looked down at his clothes.

Hearing the footsteps, the senior housekeeper emerged from the kitchen, clasping her hands together in delight.

"My word... Look how splendid you look, Master Ja-kyeong! Doesn't he look breathtaking, President Kang?"

Departing from his usual dark tactical gear and athletic wear, Jakyeong had dressed in crisp beige ankle-length trousers paired with a tailored white linen button-down. The clean lines accentuated his long, athletic limbs and lean waist—giving him an aesthetic that was strikingly pure, yet undeniably sensual.

Il-hyun’s gaze remained glued to his frame, a low, mesmerizing smile curving his lips.

"Indeed. You've managed to make me fall in love with you twice in a single day."

Jakyeong scratched the back of his neck, his cheeks warming. "Stop exaggerating."

Stepping out onto the front drive, Il-hyun walked ahead, holding the passenger door of the sleek roadster open with an exaggerated, courtly bow.

"After you, your highness."

Jakyeong let out an amused scoff, sliding into the leather bucket seat. Before he could pull the door shut, Il-hyun leaned across the center console, drawing the seatbelt across his chest.

"I have hands. I can buckle myself."

"Sit still, darling. Let me indulge in the romance of taking you out."

With a soft click of the buckle, Il-hyun rounded the hood and slipped behind the wheel, gunning the engine down the private road.

Vibrant, emerald summer foliage stretched across the rolling hills flanking the estate. Gliding along the secluded asphalt, Jakyeong began to understand why the man had established his sanctuary out here. It was completely insulated from the filth of the city. Winter must look completely different, he mused, though having only seen the estate under the summer sun, the snow-covered landscape was hard to picture.

As they merged onto the inner-city expressway, mid-afternoon traffic thickened considerably.

"Anywhere specific you'd like to go?" Il-hyun asked, keeping one hand on the wheel.

Jakyeong considered the question. Having spent his entire youth running wet-work contracts and street survival drills, the concept of leisure was completely foreign to him. He had no bucket list, no favorite cafes, and no romantic landmarks in mind.

"Not really..."

Noticing the hesitation, Il-hyun clicked open the glove compartment, retrieving a bound leather folder and passing it across.

Jakyeong flipped the cover open, only to burst into genuine laughter.

Neatly organized inside were full-color spreadsheets, categorized restaurant profiles, and mapped-out romantic itineraries detailing the premier couples' destinations across Seoul—formatted with the clinical precision of a corporate intelligence dossier.

"Who on earth put this together?"

"Tae-soo."

Jakyeong blinked. "Chief Park has experience dating?"

"Hardly. I have never seen the man speak to a romantic partner in the fifteen years he's worked for me."

Jakyeong turned his head, studying Il-hyun's sharp profile with genuine curiosity.

"What about you, President Kang? Have you had a lot of partners?"

Il-hyun offered a faint, ambiguous smirk. "What do you think?"

Jakyeong replied without a single heartbeat of hesitation:

"A serial playboy."

"Incorrect."

"A toxic degenerate?"

"Darling... that wounds me deeply."

"A complete bastard, then?"

"Do not project your personal grievances onto my romantic history."

Il-hyun laughed, shaking his head.

In truth, juggling elite academics while learning the syndicate's operational ropes throughout his twenties had left zero room for traditional romance. His past arrangements had been brief, transactional, and cold; the moment partners realized his corporate ambitions eclipsed all else, they inevitably walked away. And he had never once felt the urge to chase after a departing shadow.

Hearing the explanation, Jakyeong looked distinctly unconvinced.

"So if I tell you to let me go later on, you'll just coolly—"

Before the sentence could finish, Il-hyun cut through the air with razor-sharp finality:

"Don't even dream of it. The second you try handing me a breakup notice, you'll find yourself waking up in the afterlife."

Jakyeong scowled. "I thought you said you were cool about breakups!"

"Not with you, darling. With you, I intend to be the most petty, vindictive, obsessive monster on the planet. So wipe the thought of escaping my grip out of your head entirely."

Seeing the look of absolute, horrified despair on Jakyeong's face, Il-hyun chuckled, smoothly tossing out a parting detail:

"Did I mention I had corporate counsel revise my personal will last week?"

Why is he bringing up a last will and testament on a date?

Il-hyun turned to look at him, his dark eyes brimming with a terrifying, suffocating intensity of pure devotion.

"I added a binding clause: should I precede you in death, you are to be subjected to sunjang right beside me."

Not recognizing the archaic term, Jakyeong quickly pulled out his phone, typing the word into the search engine.

As the historical definition flashed across the screen, every drop of color drained from Jakyeong’s face.

"You're... you're joking... right?"

Il-hyun merely smiled in serene, unbothered silence.

Jakyeong demanded an immediate confirmation that it was a sick joke, but all the way down the highway, the corporate predator refused to utter a single word of denial.

Translator's Note (A/N):

  • Sunjang (순장 / 殉葬): An ancient Korean funerary custom (practiced primarily during the Three Kingdoms and Proto-Three Kingdoms periods, such as in early Buyeo, Gaya, and Silla) where living retainers, servants, concubines, or spouses were buried alive in the royal tomb alongside a deceased monarch to serve and accompany them in the afterlife. In this context, Kang Il-hyun is casually declaring in his updated will that if he dies first, Jakyeong is legally and physically required to be entombed alive in his grave with him.
